Keywords: billable hours, timekeeping, trend, time-series, utilization trend, revenue trend, monthly billings
When to Use: Tracking billable hours or collections across weeks/months; partner needs to observe rise/fall in timekeeping or revenue over a continuous fiscal period
When NOT to Use: Fewer than 4 reporting periods (use stat card); more than 6 attorneys/practice areas plotted at once (visual noise); no time dimension exists
Data Volume Threshold: <1000 pts: SVG; ≥1000 pts: Canvas + downsampling; >10000: aggregate to intervals
Color Guidance: Primary: #0080FF. Multiple series: distinct colors + distinct line styles. Fill: 20% opacity
Accessibility Notes: Differentiate series by line style (solid/dashed/dotted) not color alone. Add pattern overlays for colorblind users.
A11y Fallback: Dashed/dotted lines per series; togglable data table with timestamps and values

Keywords: caseload, attorney comparison, matters per attorney, revenue by practice area, ranking, workload
When to Use: Comparing attorneys by open matters or revenue by practice area; ranking timekeepers or practice groups is the core insight; categories <= 15
When NOT to Use: More than 15 attorneys/practice areas (use table or search); data has a time dimension (use line); showing fee mix proportions (use waffle/stacked)
Data Volume Threshold: <20 categories: vertical bar; 20–50: horizontal bar; >50: paginated table
Color Guidance: Each bar: distinct color. Grouped: same hue family. Always sort descending by value
Accessibility Notes: Value labels on each bar by default. Sort control for user reordering.
A11y Fallback: Value labels always visible; provide CSV export

Keywords: matter status, part-to-whole, case stage mix, open closed pending, proportion, share
When to Use: <=5 matter statuses (open/pending/settled/closed); one dominant status vs the rest; emphasis on visual proportion of the caseload over exact counts
When NOT to Use: More than 5 statuses; status shares differ by <5% (visually indistinguishable); user needs precise matter counts; accessibility-first context
Data Volume Threshold: Max 6 slices; beyond that switch to stacked bar 100%
Color Guidance: 5–6 max colors. Contrasting palette. Largest slice at 12 o'clock. Always label slices with %
Accessibility Notes: Pie charts fail WCAG for colorblind users. Slices rely on color alone. Avoid as primary chart in a11y contexts.
A11y Fallback: Must provide stacked bar alternative + percentage data table as mandatory fallback

Keywords: settlement correlation, time-to-resolution, case duration, distribution, outlier matters, relationship
When to Use: Exploring the relationship between two continuous case variables (e.g., settlement amount vs days-to-close); identifying outlier matters or clusters by practice area
When NOT to Use: Variables are categorical like matter type (use grouped bar); fewer than 20 matters (patterns aren't meaningful); mobile-primary context
Data Volume Threshold: <500 pts: SVG; 500–5000: Canvas at 0.6–0.8 opacity; >5000: hexbin or aggregate first
Color Guidance: Color axis: gradient (blue → red). Bubble size: relative to 3rd variable. Opacity: 0.6–0.8 to show density
Accessibility Notes: Provide data table alternative. Combine color + shape distinction for colorblind users.
A11y Fallback: Data table with correlation coefficient annotation; shape markers (circle/square/triangle) per group

Keywords: compliance heatmap, docket activity, deadline density, matrix, filings by day, calendar
When to Use: Showing compliance status or filing intensity across a 2D grid; deadline/docket patterns (e.g., filings by hour x day, or compliance status by entity x requirement)
When NOT to Use: Fewer than 20 cells (use bar); user needs to read exact filing counts; colorblind users without pattern fallback
Data Volume Threshold: Up to 10,000 cells efficiently; beyond that aggregate; calendar heatmap: 365 cells max per SVG
Color Guidance: Gradient: Cool (blue) to Hot (red). Divergent scale for ±data. Always include numeric color legend
Accessibility Notes: Pattern overlay for colorblind users. Numerical value on hover. Legend must include scale ticks.
A11y Fallback: Numerical overlay on hover; downloadable grid table with row/column labels

Keywords: jurisdiction, court filings, geographic, region, venue, spatial, choropleth
When to Use: Filing counts or matter volume have a jurisdictional/venue dimension; spatial distribution of cases across states or districts is the core insight
When NOT to Use: Jurisdictions have very different sizes making visual comparison misleading (use bar); mobile-primary context
Data Volume Threshold: <1000 regions: SVG; ≥1000: Canvas/WebGL (Deck.gl); global maps: tile-based rendering
Color Guidance: Single color gradient per region group. Categorized colors for discrete types. Legend with clear scale breaks
Accessibility Notes: Include text labels for major regions. Provide keyboard navigation between regions.
A11y Fallback: Region text labels; sortable data table by region name and value; keyboard-navigable regions

Keywords: client intake, conversion, lead funnel, drop-off, retention pipeline, stages
When to Use: Sequential intake process (inquiry -> consult -> engagement letter -> retained); showing conversion or drop-off between defined intake stages
When NOT to Use: Stages aren't sequential; values don't decrease monotonically (use bar); fewer than 3 intake stages
Data Volume Threshold: 3–8 stages optimal; beyond 8 stages group minor steps into 'Other'
Color Guidance: Stages: single color gradient (start → end). Show conversion % between each stage. Highlight biggest drop
Accessibility Notes: Explicit conversion % as text per stage. Stage labels always visible. Linear list view as fallback.
A11y Fallback: Provide linear list view with stage name + count + drop-off %; keyboard traversal

Keywords: budget vs actual, realization, matter budget, kpi, target hours, threshold, utilization
When to Use: Single matter KPI (e.g., hours logged vs budgeted, or realization rate) measured against a defined target; practice dashboard summary context
When NOT to Use: No budget or benchmark exists; comparing multiple matter KPIs at once (use bullet chart grid)
Data Volume Threshold: Single metric per gauge; for 3+ KPIs use bullet chart grid layout
Color Guidance: Performance: Red → Yellow → Green gradient. Target: marker line. Threshold zones clearly differentiated
Accessibility Notes: Always show numerical value + % of target as text beside chart. Never rely on color position alone.
A11y Fallback: Numerical value + % of target shown as visible text; ARIA live region for real-time updates

Keywords: collections forecast, revenue projection, confidence, band, billings estimate, prediction
When to Use: Historical billings + projected collections; communicating revenue uncertainty range to partners or firm management
When NOT to Use: No historical billings baseline; forecast confidence is too low to be useful; audience is not data-literate
Data Volume Threshold: Keep historical window to 30–90 days for readability; forecast horizon ≤ 30% of visible x-axis range
Color Guidance: Actual: solid line #0080FF. Forecast: dashed #FF9500. Confidence band: 15% opacity fill same hue
Accessibility Notes: Toggle between actual-only and forecast views. Legend must distinguish lines beyond color (solid vs dashed).
A11y Fallback: Toggle actual/forecast independently; legend labels must include line-style description

Keywords: trust account, anomaly, outlier, IOLTA, balance deviation, monitoring, alert
When to Use: Monitoring a trust-accounting or disbursement time-series for outliers; alerting staff to unexpected balance spikes or dips in client funds
When NOT to Use: Anomalies are predefined categories (use bar with highlight); real-time context without a pause control
Data Volume Threshold: Stream at ≤60fps with Canvas; batch: up to 10,000 pts; mark anomalies as a separate data layer
Color Guidance: Normal: #0080FF solid line. Anomaly marker: #FF0000 circle + filled. Alert band: #FFF3CD background zone
Accessibility Notes: Use shape marker (not color only) for anomaly points. Add text annotation per anomaly event.
A11y Fallback: Text alert annotation per anomaly; anomaly summary list panel alongside chart

Keywords: fee hierarchy, practice area, nested, treemap, matter type breakdown, drill
When to Use: Showing size relationships within the firm's fee hierarchy; overview of proportional structure (e.g., revenue by practice area then matter type)
When NOT to Use: Hierarchy depth > 3 levels (too complex to read); user needs to compare sibling practice-area values precisely
Data Volume Threshold: <200 nodes: SVG; 200–1000: Canvas; >1000: paginate or pre-filter before rendering
Color Guidance: Parent nodes: distinct hues. Children: lighter shades of same hue. White separator borders: 2–3px
Accessibility Notes: Poor baseline accessibility. Always provide table alternative as primary view. Label all large areas.
A11y Fallback: Collapsible tree table as primary view; treemap as supplementary visual only

Data Type: Lead Source to Practice Area Flow
Keywords: lead source, referral flow, sankey, intake distribution, source, target, transfer
When to Use: Showing how intake volume flows between lead sources and practice areas or attorneys; multi-source multi-target referral distribution
When NOT to Use: Flow directions form loops (use network graph); fewer than 3 source-target pairs; mobile-primary context
Data Volume Threshold: <50 flows: SVG; ≥50: Canvas; >200 flows: aggregate minor flows into 'Other' node
Color Guidance: Gradient from source to target color. Flow opacity: 0.4–0.6. Node labels always visible
Accessibility Notes: Structural flow charts cannot be conveyed by color alone. Provide flow table. Avoid on mobile.
A11y Fallback: Flow table (Source → Target → Value); keyboard-traversable node list with tab stops

Keywords: accounts receivable, aging, waterfall, disbursements, variance, collections bridge, delta
When to Use: Showing how individual credits/debits add up to a final balance (e.g., WIP-to-collected bridge, trust disbursements, or AR aging variance)
When NOT to Use: Changes are not additive; more than 12 bars (readability breaks); audience expects a simple total
Data Volume Threshold: 4–12 bars optimal; beyond 12 aggregate minor items into a single 'Other' bar
Color Guidance: Increases: #4CAF50. Decreases: #F44336. Start total: #2196F3. End total: #0D47A1. Running total line: dashed
Accessibility Notes: Color + directional arrow icon per bar (not color alone). Labels on every bar.
A11y Fallback: Table with running total column; directional arrow icons per row

Keywords: attorney scorecard, radar, spider, realization utilization originations, dimensions, comparison
When to Use: Comparing attorneys across the same fixed set of metrics (e.g., realization, utilization, originations, collections, client satisfaction)
When NOT to Use: Metrics > 8 (unreadable); values need precise comparison (use grouped bar); audience unfamiliar with radar charts
Data Volume Threshold: 2–3 datasets maximum per chart; 5–8 axes; beyond 8 axes switch to parallel coordinates
Color Guidance: Single dataset: #0080FF at 20% fill. Multiple: distinct hues with 30% fill. Border: full opacity
Accessibility Notes: Limit axes to 5–8. Always provide grouped bar chart alternative for precise reading.
A11y Fallback: Grouped bar chart as mandatory alternative; include raw data table

Keywords: settlement negotiation, offer range, ohlc, open high low close, litigation finance, valuation
When to Use: Financial-style time-series of negotiation rounds with Open/High/Low/Close offers, or daily case-valuation ranges; litigation finance context only
When NOT to Use: Non-financial audience; no OHLC/range data available (use line chart); accessibility-first context
Data Volume Threshold: Real-time: Canvas required. Historical: paginate by time range. Max 500 candles visible at once
Color Guidance: Bullish: #26A69A. Bearish: #EF5350. Volume bars: 40% opacity below. Body fill vs hollow for OHLC style
Accessibility Notes: Provide OHLC data table. Colorblind: use fill vs outline pattern (bullish = filled, bearish = hollow).
A11y Fallback: OHLC data table with sortable columns; numeric summary panel (daily change %)

Keywords: referral network, graph, nodes, edges, co-counsel connections, relationships, force
When to Use: Mapping referral relationships between clients, co-counsel, and referral sources; referral network topology exploration context
When NOT to Use: Node count > 500 without clustering pre-applied; user needs precise referral counts; mobile context
Data Volume Threshold: ≤100 nodes: SVG; 101–500: Canvas; >500: must apply clustering/LOD before rendering
Color Guidance: Node types: categorical colors. Edges: #90A4AE at 60% opacity. Highlight path: #F59E0B
Accessibility Notes: Fundamentally inaccessible without alternative. Never use as sole representation. Always provide list alternative.
A11y Fallback: Adjacency list table (Node A → Node B → Weight); hierarchical tree view when structure allows

Keywords: verdict amounts, settlement distribution, spread, median award, outlier, quartile, boxplot
When to Use: Showing spread, median, and outliers of settlement or verdict amounts; comparing award distributions across practice areas or venues
When NOT to Use: Fewer than 20 matters per group (distribution is not meaningful); audience unfamiliar with statistical charts
Data Volume Threshold: Any sample size; aggregated representation so rendering is ⚡ Excellent at any volume
Color Guidance: Box fill: #BBDEFB. Border: #1976D2. Median line: #D32F2F bold. Outlier dots: #F44336
Accessibility Notes: Include stats summary table. Annotate outlier count in chart subtitle.
A11y Fallback: Stats summary table (min / Q1 / median / Q3 / max / mean); outlier count annotation

Keywords: realization, utilization, bullet, compact, attorney kpi, dashboard, benchmark, range
When to Use: Dashboard with multiple attorney or practice-area KPIs (realization, utilization, collections) side by side; space-constrained contexts where a gauge is too large
When NOT to Use: Single KPI with emphasis (use gauge); metric has no defined target range; fewer than 3 KPIs
Data Volume Threshold: Ideal for 3–10 bullet charts in a grid; scales to any count efficiently
Color Guidance: Qualitative ranges: #FFCDD2 / #FFF9C4 / #C8E6C9 (bad/ok/good). Performance bar: #1976D2. Target: black 3px marker
Accessibility Notes: All values always visible as text. Color ranges are labeled with text thresholds not color alone.
A11y Fallback: Numerical values always visible (not hover-only); color ranges labeled with threshold text

Keywords: e-discovery, document review, waffle, percentage, completion, filled, grid
When to Use: Showing what fraction of a document review set is complete; e-discovery or contract-review progress in a visually engaging and accessible format
When NOT to Use: More than 5 review categories (use stacked bar); exact document counts matter over visual proportion; very tight space
Data Volume Threshold: 10×10 grid standard (100 cells); for > 5 categories switch to stacked 100% bar
Color Guidance: 3–5 categories max. 2–3px gap between cells. Each category a distinct accessible color pair
Accessibility Notes: Better than pie for accessibility. Percentage text label always visible. Each cell has aria-label.
A11y Fallback: Percentage text always visible; grid cells labeled with aria-label value; provide legend

Keywords: revenue breakdown, sunburst, department, practice area, nested, radial, proportion
When to Use: Exploring nested revenue proportions where both hierarchy and relative size matter (e.g., department -> practice area -> matter type spend)
When NOT to Use: More than 3 hierarchy levels (outer rings become unreadable); precision matters over overview; mobile
Data Volume Threshold: <100 nodes: SVG; 100–500: Canvas; >500: filter to top N before rendering
Color Guidance: Center to outer: darker to lighter hue. Each level 15–20% lighter. Contrasting border between sectors
Accessibility Notes: Poor accessibility beyond 2 levels. Mandatory table alternative required for any production use.
A11y Fallback: Collapsible indented list with percentages; breadcrumb trail for current drill-down state

Keywords: root cause, realization decline, decomposition, tree, drill-down, write-off attribution
When to Use: Decomposing a firm metric (e.g., falling realization or collections) into contributing factors; BI drill-down or AI-assisted practice analysis
When NOT to Use: No clear parent-child causal relationship; audience expects a summary rather than exploration
Data Volume Threshold: Up to 5 levels deep; limit visible nodes to 20 per level for readability; lazy-load deeper levels
Color Guidance: Positive impact nodes: #2563EB. Negative impact nodes: #EF4444. Neutral connectors: #94A3B8
Accessibility Notes: Keyboard-navigable expand/collapse. Screen reader announces node value and % contribution.
A11y Fallback: Keyboard expand/collapse tree; screen reader announces node label + value + % impact

Keywords: 3d, evidence, accident reconstruction, spatial, litigation exhibit, volumetric, point-cloud
When to Use: Litigation-support context where a Z-axis carries essential info (e.g., accident-scene or forensic reconstruction exhibits) not expressible in 2D
When NOT to Use: 2D projection conveys the same insight; mobile context; accessibility-required environments; standard practice dashboards
Data Volume Threshold: WebGL required. Deck.gl: up to 1M points. Three.js: LOD required beyond 50,000 pts
Color Guidance: Depth cues: lighting and shading. Z-axis: color gradient (cool → warm). Transparent overlapping: opacity 0.4
Accessibility Notes: 3D spatial charts are fundamentally inaccessible. Must not be used as primary chart type in any product UI.
A11y Fallback: Mandatory 2D projection view + data table; do not use as primary chart type in product UI

Keywords: streaming, real-time, docket, live filings, review rate, pulse, monitoring
When to Use: Live litigation-ops dashboards; docket-alert or e-discovery review-rate data updating at >=1 Hz; user needs the current value at a glance
When NOT to Use: Update frequency < 1/min (use periodic-refresh line chart); flashing content without reduced-motion support
Data Volume Threshold: Canvas/WebGL required. Buffer last 60–300s of data. Downsample older data on scroll
Color Guidance: Current pulse: #00FF00 (dark theme) or #0080FF (light theme). History: fading opacity. Grid: dark background
Accessibility Notes: Pause/resume control required. Current value as large visible text KPI. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
A11y Fallback: Pause/resume button required; current value shown as large text KPI; prefers-reduced-motion: freeze animation

Keywords: sentiment, deposition, contract clause, nlp, opinion, tone, text-analysis
When to Use: NLP output on legal text (deposition transcripts, contract clauses, client reviews); frequency-weighted keyword overview of a legal corpus
When NOT to Use: Precise values matter (word size is inherently imprecise); screen-reader context; corpus < 50 items
Data Volume Threshold: 50–5000 terms optimal. Beyond 5000: apply top-N filtering before render. Avoid on mobile
Color Guidance: Positive: #22C55E. Negative: #EF4444. Neutral: #94A3B8. Word size maps to frequency
Accessibility Notes: Word clouds fail screen readers. Never use as sole output of NLP analysis. Always pair with list view.
A11y Fallback: Sortable list view by frequency with sentiment label column; word cloud as supplementary only

Keywords: process mining, matter lifecycle, variants, workflow path, bottleneck, event log, deviation
When to Use: Analyzing matter or intake event logs to visualize actual case workflows; identifying bottlenecks and deviations in the matter lifecycle
When NOT to Use: No event log data available; audience expects a static flowchart (use diagram tool); node count > 100 without pre-filtering
Data Volume Threshold: <30 nodes: SVG; 30–100: Canvas; >100: apply variant filtering (top 80% of cases) before rendering
Color Guidance: Happy path: #10B981 thick line. Deviations: #F59E0B thin line. Bottleneck nodes: #EF4444 fill
Accessibility Notes: Complex graphs are hard to navigate. Provide path summary text. Highlight top 3 bottlenecks as annotations.
A11y Fallback: Path summary table (variant → frequency → avg duration); top 3 bottlenecks as text annotation panel
